snapshot: WHO African Region. The federal ministry sets policy and channels funds through the Basic Health Care Provision Fund, while state governments carry most service delivery and outbreak response. Nigeria confirmed its first imported Ebola case (Bundibugyo virus) in October 2026.

agenda.title: Containing the imported Ebola case
agenda.text: Nigeria confirmed one imported Bundibugyo Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory, a woman who had travelled from Uganda. Minister Pate called the case contained and said airport surveillance was stepped up. In its update of 10 November the NCDC reported no further confirmed cases 21 days after confirmation: 62 contacts were identified, 34 have finished 21 days of monitoring and 28 remain under surveillance.

agenda.title: Health sector renewal and the sector-wide approach
agenda.text: The Nigerian Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative, run as a sector-wide approach, is the government's main reform programme. It attracted about US$3 billion in external funding and covers primary care upgrades, health worker training, health security, insurance enrolment and local production of medicines. At the second Joint Annual Review in November 2025 the government said it plans to double the share of federal revenue going to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund from 1% to 2% and asked states to put in counterpart funding.

agenda.title: Health insurance and financial protection
agenda.text: In February 2026 Minister of State Salako said out-of-pocket payments make up 71% of total health spending and that national health insurance covers roughly 10% to 13% of the population, with more than 20 million people enrolled. The government plans to step up enforcement of mandatory insurance for federal agencies, following an executive order from President Tinubu, and aims to beat its 2027 coverage target of 20%.

agenda.title: Lassa fever and other outbreaks
agenda.text: During the 2026 Lassa fever peak season the NCDC warned of rising cases in 18 states, with 28 health workers infected, and asked governors to activate state incident management systems and release response funds. Its November update also flags dengue in Sokoto and Zamfara, chikungunya in Sokoto, diphtheria and cerebrospinal meningitis.

nl.text: The Netherlands and Nigeria signed an agreement on an autologous blood service in March 2024; further Dutch links come from the NPHI Collaboration Map.

items.title: Agreement on tackling blood shortages (autologous blood service)
items.who: Nigerian Federal Ministry of Health, the Netherlands (Deputy Minister for Public Health), National Blood Service Commission and HemoClear
items.text: Sets up a service that processes a patient's own blood during surgery so it can be transfused back, to ease shortages and keep donated blood for conditions such as sickle cell disease and cancer. The partnership is financed by the French Fund for Innovation in Development.
